Bug_Details: Calling Iterator.hasNext() is not supposed to have any side effects and hence should not change the iterator’s state. Iterator.next() advances the iterator by one item. So calling it inside Iterator.hasNext() breaks the hasNext() contract and will lead to unexpected behavior in production.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is caused by calling iterator.next() inside iterator.hasNext(). This call advances the iterator, which is incorrect and violates the expected behavior of hasNext().
Trigger_Explanation: The test case called showBug with a list of integers. The bug is triggered because the implementation of showBug incorrectly uses iterator.next() within iterator.hasNext(), which advances the iterator upon each call and hence skips elements. The test expects the original list to be returned, but due to the bug, it fails.
